AnonymousObjectElement.Definition: An element supplied to an anonymous object creation expression.

Argument.Definition: A value passed to a method or constructor when its invoked. Arguments are passed into the corresponding parameters in the method or constructor definition so they can be used in that context.

AssignmentValue.Definition: The value assigned to a variable, field, or property by an assignment or initializer expression.

AttributeArgument.Definition: Attribute arguments provide values to an attribute. They configure how the attribute behaves or supplies additional information.

CastTarget.Definition: A cast target is the value being converted to a new type.

CollectionElement.Definition: A value or expression supplied as an element within a collection expression or initializer.

CollectionElementKey.Definition: This value identifies an entry inside a key-value collection, such as a {c:color-green code}Dictionary{/c}. This key can be used later to find the value associated with it.

CollectionElementValue.Definition: This value is the data stored inside a key-value collection entry. In a {c:color-green code}Dictionary{/c}, this is the value returned when the matching key is looked up.

CollectionLength.Definition: A value that specifies the number of elements in a newly created collection or span.

IndexValue.Definition: An expression that specifies a position or offset used in an index or range when accessing a sequence.

InterpolatedValue.Definition: An interpolated value is an expression embedded inside an interpolated string. Its result is inserted into the string at runtime.

NullCoalescingAssignmentValue.Definition: The value assigned to the target variable in a null-coalescing assignment (??=) when the target is null.

QueryReturnValue.Definition: A value returned by a query expression.

ReturnValue.Definition: The result produced by a method or function that is sent back to the caller when execution finishes.

SwitchArmValue.Definition: The expression produced by a switch expression arm when its pattern matches.

SwitchMatchTarget.Definition: The expression whose value is matched against the patterns of a switch expression.

AddressOfOperand.Definition: The variable or location whose address is obtained by the address-of operator (&).

ArithmeticOperand.Definition: A numeric value participating in an arithmetic expression, combined with another operand using an arithmetic operator.

ComparisonOperand.Definition: A value in a comparison expression, evaluated against another operand using a relational or equality operator.

ConcatenationOperand.Definition: A value combined with another operand using the string concatenation operator to produce a single composed string.

DefaultOperand.Definition: The type supplied to the {c:color-blue keyword}default{/c} operator.

DereferenceOperand.Definition: The pointer expression whose referenced value is accessed by the dereference operator (*).

LogicalOperand.Definition: A boolean value participating in a logical expression, combined with another operand using a logical operator.

NameOfOperand.Definition: The type supplied to the {c:color-blue keyword}nameof{/c} operator.

NullCoalescingFallback.Definition: The value returned by a null-coalescing expression when the target value is null.

NullCoalescingTarget.Definition: The value evaluated for null in a null-coalescing expression. If it is not null, it becomes the result of the expression.

NullForgivingOperand.Definition: The expression whose null-state is overridden by the null-forgiving operator (!), forcing the compiler to treat it as non-null.

SizeOfOperand.Definition: The type supplied to the {c:color-blue keyword}sizeof{/c} operator to determine its compile-time memory size in bytes.

TernaryTrueValue.Definition: The value returned when the value or condition preceding the {c:keyword}?{/c} evaluates to {c:color-blue keyword}true{/c}.

TernaryFalseValue.Definition: The value returned by a ternary expression when the condition evaluates to false.

TypeOfOperand.Definition: The type supplied to the {c:color-blue keyword}typeof{/c} operator to obtain its runtime {c:color-gray keyword}System.Type{/c} representation.

ConstantPattern.Definition: A constant pattern specifies a constant value being checked in a pattern matching expression.

PatternBindingVariable.Definition: A variable introduced by a pattern that is assigned the matched value or a component of it when the pattern succeeds.

PatternMatchTarget.Definition: The expression whose runtime value is tested against a pattern in an is expression or switch pattern match.

PropertyPattern.Definition: A property name token within a property pattern that specifies which member of the matched value is evaluated against a nested pattern.

RelationalPattern.Definition: A constant or expression token in a relational pattern that is compared to the matched value using a relational operator (>, <, >=, <=).

TypePattern.Definition: A type pattern specifies the type being checked in a pattern matching expression. It determines whether a value matches a given type.

VarPattern.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}var{/c} keyword in a pattern that matches any value and introduces a binding variable for that value or a component of it.

TypeQualifier.Definition: A type qualifier identifies a specific type within a namespace or enclosing type. It helps precisely locate the type being referenced.

ArrayBaseType.Definition: The data type supported by the array. The base type and array-type indicators [] make up the full data type.

CastType.Definition: A cast type specifies the type that a value is being converted to. It is used when explicitly changing how a value is treated in code.

DeconstructionVariableType.Definition: The data type a variable will have after it has been deconstructed.

DelegateReturnType.Definition: A delegate return type defines the type of value returned by methods that match the delegate. It specifies what result the delegate’s methods must produce.

FieldType.Definition: A field data type defines what kind of data a field can store. It determines the values that can be assigned to the field.

Loop Iterator Type.Definition: The data type of the iterator variable declared in a {c:color-purple keyword}for{/c} or {c:color-purple keyword}foreach{/c} loop.

GenericTypeArgument.Definition: A generic type argument is a specific type supplied to a generic class or method. It fills in the placeholder defined by a generic parameter.

LocalFunctionReturnType.Definition: Defines the type of value returned by a {c:bold}local function{/c}.

LocalVariableType.Definition: A local variable data type defines what kind of value a local variable can hold. It determines how the variable can be used within its scope.

MethodReturnType.Definition: This part of the method signature defines what data will be returned when the method is finished executing.

ParameterType.Definition: A parameter data type defines what kind of value can be passed into a method or constructor. It ensures the argument matches the expected type.

PointerBaseType.Definition: The underlying type in a pointer type declaration, indicating the type of value the pointer can reference.

PropertyType.Definition: A property data type defines what kind of value a property can get or set. It controls the type of data exposed by the property.

TupleElement.Definition: A single element inside a {c:bold}tuple{/c} expression. Each element holds one position in the tuple and can represent a value, a type, or a named entry depending on how the tuple is being used.

TupleElementType.Definition: A tuple element type defines the type of a value stored in a tuple. It determines what kind of data that element can hold.

TypeConstraint.Definition: A type constraint restricts what types can be used with a generic type or method. It helps ensure that only valid types are allowed.

TypeParameterConstraint.Definition: This identifier references the declared generic type parameter inside a constraint clause that sets rules for the arguments that are allowed to be passed in for the generic type parameter.
